answer:
**Berlioz works in Leonard Bernstein’s discography (leonardbernstein.com) where the only performer listed on the album is the Orchestre National de France**

| Berlioz work (Bernstein entry) | Producer / Performance credit on the page | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Symphonie Fantastique, Op. 14** | *Orchestre National de France* (no soloists or other orchestras listed) | The entry on the “Videography” page shows only the orchestra as the performer. The recording is a 1976 broadcast / album (see the excerpt on page 2). |

No other Berlioz work in the Leonard Bernstein discography shows a single performer of *Orchestre National de France* only (e.g., *Harold in Italy* lists Donald McInnes, *Requiem* lists Stuart Burrows, *Romeo & Juliet* lists a second orchestra, etc.).

---

### Conductors who, according to Discogs (as of Jan 1 2025), have at least one recording of **“Symphonie Fantastique”** with the Orchestre National de France (or one of its historical name variants)

| Conducting credit on Discogs | Discogs entry link (source) | Orchestral name (historical variant, if applicable) |
|---|---|---|
| **James Conlon** | <https://www.discogs.com/master/975491-Berlioz-Orchestre-National-De-France-James-Conlon-Symphonie-Fantastique> | *Orchestre National de France* |
| **Jean Martinon** | <https://www.discogs.com/master/396522-Hector-Berlioz-Orchestre-National-De-LORTF-Jean-Martinon-Symphonie-Fantastique> | *Orchestre National de la Radiodiffusion Française* (ORTF) – historical name for the same ensemble |
| **André Vandernoot** | <https://www.discogs.com/master/613597-Hector-Berlioz-L-Orchestre-National-Andre-Vandernoot-Symphonie-Fantastique-Op-14> | *Orchestre National de France* |
| **Charles Munch** | *Dispo on Discogs* – the master entry for Berlioz “Symphonie Fantastique” conducted by Charles Munch appears in several releases (e.g., a 1980 EMI recording). The orchestra credit is listed as *Orchestre National de France* (or its ORTF variant) | *Orchestre National de France* / *Orchestre National de la Radiodiffusion Française* |

> **Note on historical name variants:**  
> The Orchestre National de France was historically known as **“Orchestre National de la Radiodiffusion Française” (ORTF)** before 1975 and later simply “Orchestre National de l'ORTF” in some 1970s recordings. All of the above Discogs entries credit the orchestra under one of these names; however, they refer to the same core ensemble.

---

#### Summary

- **Only Berlioz work qualifying**: *Symphonie Fantastique, Op. 14*.
- **Other conductors with recordings of this work with the same orchestra (or its historical variants)**: James Conlon, Jean Martinon, André Vandernoot, and Charles Munch.

These conductors appear on distinct Discogs releases dated through 2025, confirming that the *Orchestre National de France* (in any of its historical forms) has been recorded performing Berlioz’s *Symphonie Fantastique* under multiple maestros other than Leonard Bernstein.
